To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mouse HP gene promoter is a complex regulatory element that contains multiple species-specific binding sites.
(1) the acute phase reaction is conserved in the mouse, (2) the IL-1 response in the mouse HP gene is species specific, and (3) the PEA3 protein may be a key regulator of mouse HP gene transcription.
the HP gene promoter is responsive to glucocorticoids in both mouse species, and that IL-1 response in M. caroi is mediated by a PEA3 binding site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of species-specific regulation of HP expression.
the evolution of the acute phase response in rodents.
the evolution of the regulatory elements of the mouse HP gene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mouse HP gene is a good model for the human gene.
in mouse hepatocytes IL-1 and glucocorticoids are the most important regulators of the HP gene, whereas in human hepatocytes IL-6 is the most important.
there are species-specific differences in the regulation of HP genes in mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
species-specific differences in the regulation of HP are caused by changes in the regulatory elements, whereas the basic structure of the gene remains conserved.
the HP gene of the Mus species has a strong glucocorticoid response element, a weak IL-6 response element, and a weak IL-1 response element.
in mouse, glucocorticoid is the major stimulator of HP gene expression, whereas in rat and human, IL-1 is also a potent stimulatory agent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the species-specific changes in the HP regulatory elements are responsible for the different hormone requirements of HP gene expression in the mouse.
there are species-specific differences in regulatory elements of murine HP gene.
species-specific differences in the regulation of acute phase proteins can be attributed to differences in regulatory elements in the gene promoter.
